question: Among the stars within 32 light-years of the Sun, what share are small, dim red dwarfs?
answer: About three in four. In the Gaia-era census of stars within 32 light-years, about 250 of 340 are red dwarfs. Yet not one is easy to see without a telescope: the brightest, AX Microscopii, sits at the very limit of perfect skies. The night sky is a catalogue of the rare, bright few.
move: The easiest members to see are rarely the typical ones.
trap: The naked-eye sky has almost no red dwarfs, so they seem rare.
